chunks: Muhammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Ḥusain narrated to me, saying: Ḥasan ibn ‘Ali ibn Mahziyār narrated to me from his father, from Ḥusayn ibn Sa‘īd, from Zur‘ah ibn Muḥammad al-Ḥaḍrami, from al-Mufaḍḍal ibn ‘Umar,

Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) said: ‘Going to the Ziyārah is better than not going, and not going is better than going.’ I said, ‘You broke my back!’ He said: ‘By Allāh, one of you goes to the grave of his father anguished and grieved, but you come to him (Imam al-Ḥusayn) with provisions (food). No! Unless you come to him disheveled and covered with dust.’

key_terms.تَزُورُونَ: Ziyārah (visitation, specifically of graves or shrines)

ai.seo_question: What is the proper spiritual state and etiquette when visiting the grave of Imam al-Husayn?
ai.summary: In *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, Ibn Qulawayh records Imam al-Ṣādiq (a.s.) contrasting the solemn, grief-stricken visit to one's own father with the often superficial, provision-laden visits to Imam al-Ḥusayn (a.s.). The Imam emphasizes that true *ziyarah* requires shedding worldly comforts to appear 'disheveled and dusty' (*shuʿthān ghubran*), mirroring the raw spiritual humility of the Ahl al-Bayt. This highlights the Shia scholarly view that the physical state of the visitor should reflect the internal state of mourning for the Imam's sacrifice.
